answer: Sequential Worktime Accumulation. Each identity earns write-access only after completing a verifiable compute task tied to a slow-release schedule, like water filling a vault one drop per hour. The rate is capped per hardware fingerprint, so parallel identities each need separate idle machines. An attacker must sustain real uptime across thousands of nodes, an oasis of usable capacity drowning in maintenance cost. Sybil clusters starve on the glacier of withheld rewards that unlock only after months of continuous history.
